messages.subject: SNPs dropped dramatically with more files using sumstats() function
messages.subject_clean: SNPs dropped dramatically with more files using sumstats() function
messages.body_plain:
Hi Group,

Does anyone kindly have a clue for the issue blew? Any comments would be greatly appreciated!

I was using the sumstats() function to prepare for a GWAS GSEM. However lots more of SNPs dropped as I included more summary stats files in the sumstats() function .

I found that a SNP in all 30 files and the reference file could also be dropped as I increased the number of files from 3 to 30. This SNP has no MAF issue on the reference file.

This is so wired.

Thanks so much,
YC

messages.subject: Deflated GWAS associations
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I seem to get very deflated latent factor GWAS associations for some factors from models with everything from 4 to 10 latent factors with variance explained from .57 to .76. Was wondering if you have seen this as well. Do you have any thoughts on re-inflation procedures for GWAS or how justified it is to use them?

Kind regards,
Johan

messages.subject: Re: Deflated GWAS associations
messages.body_plain:
If the factor model is wrong, such that there is very high Q_SNP, then the mean chisq for snp associations from a common factor gwas are expected to be relatively low.  We see this for the p factor in the following preprint.
Grotzinger, A. D., …Tucker-Drob, E. M., & Nivard, M. G. (2020). Genetic architecture of 11 major psychiatric disorders at biobehavioral, functional genomic, and molecular genetic levels of analysis. medRχiv [Tucker-Drob & Nivard jointly directed this work] Link <https://doi.org/10.1101/2020.09.22.20196089>
The point is that a factor model will not necessarily increase association power if the model is inappropriate for the data at the level of the SNPs. I would suggest taking a close look at the preprint as it is instructive.

messages.subject: Association threshold.
messages.body_plain:
Good morning,

I am fitting markers in my SEM analysis. Could you tell me how I can determine a p-value threshold for my association.? I use permutation for this matters usually, but for genomicSEM seems to be an issue since the time required to finished my association was quite long and it will be even longer if I am planning to do thousands of permutations.

Best,

Joel

messages.subject: Re: Association threshold.
messages.body_plain:
The field standard in human genetics for associations involving individual markers is 5x10^-8. Genomic SEM provides SEs based on a multivariate block jacknife from ldsc, so a permutation is typically not conducted. p values can be derived from the Z statistics based on the normal distribution.

messages.subject: Re: error message
messages.body_plain:
This is a common factor gwas? do you get this error for just a few snps? have you looked at the individual SNP effects on the factor indicators from the univariate sumstats? are they exactly 0? is there a Z statistic that is exactly 0? you'd need to do a bit of detective work to figure out why there is basically a matrix that is univertable. looking at the additional warnings might also provide clues.
If it's just a few snps out of millions it might be justified to remove them as part of QC loss... hard to say more based on the contents of your email.
